stem: When following a regurgitating infant over time, which change should most clearly prompt reconsideration of uncomplicated gastro-oesophageal reflux and further assessment?

options.text: Regurgitation continues but the child is growing normally
Poor growth becomes apparent alongside regurgitation
Regurgitation began in the first 2 months of life

explanation: Poor growth alongside regurgitation is the concerning change. This suggests the infant may no longer have uncomplicated reflux and should be reassessed for an underlying problem.

citations.title: Louisa Leone MD3 2025 - Child and Adolescent Health - Study Notes.pdf

optionExplanations.A: Incorrect because normal growth supports uncomplicated gastro-oesophageal reflux.
optionExplanations.B: Incorrect because symptoms that improve with age fit the usual course of uncomplicated reflux.
optionExplanations.C: Correct because poor growth with regurgitation is a red flag that should prompt further assessment.
optionExplanations.D: Incorrect because onset in the first 2 months of life is compatible with typical infant reflux.
optionExplanations.E: Incorrect because frequent episodes alone can still occur in uncomplicated reflux.
